newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gold seen slipping further in nervous market.
newsitem.headline: Gold seen slipping further in nervous market.

text.p: Gold began lower in Europe and could fall further after plunging to 12-year lows last week on news of Australian central bank gold sales, dealers said on Monday.
Trading was edgy and quiet in Europe, with the market getting some support from physical demand at these levels.

But prices should again come under pressure in the afternoon, when U.S. trading begins, and overnight in the Far East on worries that other central banks will also begin selling gold, one analyst said.
The Reserve Bank of Australia last week confirmed that it sold 167 tonnes of gold from reserves in the past six months.
"I'm reluctant to say where gold could go. We are already five dollars lower (from Friday) and $300 is not far away," one dealer said.
Gold began at $318.85/$319.35 an ounce, after $324.25/$324.75 at Friday's London close.
Technical analysts saw the next support level for gold at $310.
Silver was a little steadier as it tried to hold the $4.50 level, and platinum and palladium prices were still being supported by Russia's delivery problems, dealers also said.
Silver opened at $4.51/$4.53, versus $4.54/$4.56, while platinum was at $418.00/$422.00, against $419.00/$422.00, and palladium slipped three dollars to $187.00/$191.00.
